docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Base URL: /api

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Method Path Purpose GET /health Check API and database availability GET /products List saved products POST /products Create a product GET /nutrition-overview Return day-grouped totals for one deviceId POST /day-entries Create a logged food entry DELETE /day-entries/:id Delete a logged food entry

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text:
• success: HTTP 200 with { "status": "ok" }
  • failure: HTTP 503 with { "status": "error" }

docs.title: GET /products
docs.text:
• returns up to 100 products ordered by name
  • response shape: { "products": [...] }

Example item:

{
  "id": "cm123...",
  "name": "Banana",
  "servingSize": "100 g",
  "calories": 89,
  "protein": 1.1,
  "fat": 0.3,
  "carbs": 22.8
}

docs.title: POST /products
docs.text:
Request body:

{
  "name": "Banana",
  "servingSize": "100 g",
  "calories": 89,
  "protein": 1.1,
  "fat": 0.3,
  "carbs": 22.8
}

Rules:

  • name is required
  • nutrition values must be non-negative numbers
  • servingSize defaults to 100 g

Success: HTTP 201 with { "product": ... }

docs.title: GET /nutrition-overview
docs.text:
Query parameters:

Parameter Required Description deviceId Yes Browser identity key timezoneOffsetMinutes Yes Used for day grouping

Example request:

curl "http://localhost:3000/api/nutrition-overview?deviceId=demo-device&timezoneOffsetMinutes=-120"

Response shape:

  • overview.days contains grouped entries by date key
  • overview.dailyCalorieIndicators contains calendar indicators
  • overview.defaultDay and overview.defaultIndicator are fallbacks

Failure cases:

  • HTTP 400 when deviceId is missing
  • HTTP 400 when timezoneOffsetMinutes is invalid

docs.title: POST /day-entries
docs.text:
Request body:

{
  "productId": "cm123...",
  "amount": 125,
  "eatenAt": "2026-05-31T08:00:00.000Z",
  "deviceId": "demo-device"
}

Rules:

  • productId, amount, eatenAt, and deviceId are required
  • amount must be non-negative
  • eatenAt must be a valid date

Success: HTTP 201 with { "dayEntry": ... }

Failure cases:

  • HTTP 400 for invalid input
  • HTTP 404 if the product does not exist

docs.title: DELETE /day-entries/:id
docs.text:
Deletes one stored day entry.

Success: HTTP 204 No Content

docs.title: Generic server error
docs.text:
Unexpected failures return HTTP 500 with:

{
  "error": "Internal server error."
}

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Nutrio uses a small client-server setup with minimal layers.

docs.title: System map
docs.text:
React frontend
    |
    v
Nginx
    |
    v
Express API
    |
    v
Prisma + PostgreSQL

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
The frontend is responsible for:

  • screen navigation
  • product and overview requests
  • creating and deleting day entries

It also stores a persistent deviceId in localStorage and sends timezoneOffsetMinutes with overview requests.

docs.title: Backend
docs.text:
The API is responsible for:

  • health checks
  • product creation and listing
  • nutrition overview aggregation
  • day entry creation and deletion

The nutrition logic converts product values from per 100 g into entry totals and compares the result with built-in daily targets.

docs.title: Core flow
docs.text:
1. The frontend sends requests to /api.
  2. The API validates data and reads or writes through Prisma.
  3. PostgreSQL stores products and day entries.
  4. The frontend refreshes the visible totals.

docs.title: Product
docs.text:
• name
  • serving size
  • calories
  • protein
  • fat
  • carbs

docs.title: DayEntry
docs.text:
• copied product name
  • amount in grams
  • calculated nutrition values
  • deviceId
  • eatenAt

docs.title: Identity model
docs.text: Nutrio does not use accounts. Data is separated by a browser-generated deviceId.

docs.title: Runtime services
docs.text:
The Docker setup runs four services:

  • frontend
  • api
  • db
  • pgadmin

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: Nutrio is deployed as a small Docker-based stack.

docs.title: Services
docs.text: Service Purpose frontend Serves the built frontend through Nginx api Runs Prisma migrations and starts the Express API db Stores products and day entries pgadmin Optional database UI

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
Port Use 8080 Main app 5050 pgAdmin

The API stays inside the Docker network and is reached through Nginx.

docs.title: Container behavior
docs.text:
• the frontend image builds dist/ and serves it with Nginx
  • the API image generates the Prisma client and starts the server
  • the API container runs npm run prisma:migrate:deploy on startup

docs.title: Before publishing
docs.text:
• set real values in .env
  • confirm PostgreSQL data is persistent
  • confirm /api/health returns 200
  • confirm frontend routing works after refresh

docs.title: Production notes
docs.text:
For a more serious deployment, consider:

  • authentication
  • backups
  • structured logs
  • monitoring
  • restricted access to pgAdmin

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Nutrio can be started in two ways:

  • Docker Compose for the fastest end-to-end setup
  • Local development if you want to run the frontend and API separately

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Tool Why it is needed Node.js 22 Required for local frontend and API execution npm Used for package installation and scripts Docker Required for the containerized workflow PostgreSQL Required only for local API development outside Docker

docs.title: Fastest path: Docker Compose
docs.text:
Recommended for first run

If your goal is to try the app quickly, start with Docker. It gives you the frontend, API, database, and pgAdmin in one command.

docker composedocker-compose 
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up --build

cp .env.example .env
docker-compose up --build

After startup, these endpoints should be available:

Service URL App http://localhost:8080 pgAdmin http://localhost:5050 API health check http://localhost:8080/api/health

docs.title: What the Docker setup does
docs.text:
• Builds the Vite frontend and serves it through nginx:1.27-alpine
  • Starts the API on port 3000 inside the Docker network
  • Starts PostgreSQL 16
  • Runs npm run prisma:migrate:deploy when the API container starts
  • Exposes pgAdmin for database inspection

docs.title: Local development
docs.text: Use this path if you want live frontend development with Vite and direct control of the API process.

docs.title: 1. Install dependencies
docs.text: npm install

docs.title: 2. Provide a PostgreSQL connection
docs.text:
The local API reads DATABASE_URL from the shell environment. It does not load .env automatically, so export the variable before starting the API.

Example:

export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://nutrio:change_me_to_a_strong_password@localhost:5432/nutrio?schema=public"

docs.title: 3. Generate the Prisma client and run migrations
docs.text:
npm run prisma:generate
npm run prisma:migrate:deploy

docs.title: 4. Start the API
docs.text: npm run api:start

docs.title: 5. Start the frontend in another terminal
docs.text:
npm run dev

The Vite frontend runs on http://localhost:5173 and proxies /api requests to http://localhost:3000.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Used by Purpose POSTGRES_DB Docker Compose Database name for the PostgreSQL container POSTGRES_USER Docker Compose Database user for the PostgreSQL container POSTGRES_PASSWORD Docker Compose Database password for the PostgreSQL container PGADMIN_DEFAULT_EMAIL Docker Compose Login email for pgAdmin PGADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD Docker Compose Login password for pgAdmin DATABASE_URL Local API and Prisma Direct PostgreSQL connection string

docs.title: First-run checklist
docs.text:
• Open the app and confirm the main screens Today, Add, and Products
  • Create one product on the Add screen
  • Log that product into any meal section on the Today screen
  • Confirm GET /api/health returns { "status": "ok" }

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
npm run build
npm run prisma:generate
npm run prisma:migrate:deploy

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Common issues in the current Nutrio setup.

Problem What to check DATABASE_URL is required Export DATABASE_URL before starting the local API /api/health returns 503 PostgreSQL is running and credentials are correct Frontend shows 502 for API calls API container is running and passed its health check Data is missing in another browser Nutrio separates data by browser deviceId Entries appear on the wrong day Client timezone and clock are correct Prisma migrations fail Database connectivity and migration target are correct Product creation returns 400 Required nutrition fields are filled with valid numbers

docs.title: Example fix for local API startup
docs.text:
export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://nutrio:change_me_to_a_strong_password@localhost:5432/nutrio?schema=public"
npm run api:start

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: This section is for using Nutrio as an app.

docs.title: Use it if you want to
docs.text:
• create and save food products
  • log meals for the current day
  • review calories and macronutrients
  • switch between days in the calendar
  • remove an incorrect entry

docs.title: Start here
docs.text: Read Using Nutrio, then open the app and try one full flow: create a product, log a meal, and verify the totals.

docs.title: Need technical details?
docs.text: If you need installation, Docker, API, or architecture details, go to Developer Guide.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: This guide follows the normal user workflow inside Nutrio.

docs.title: Main screens
docs.text: Screen Purpose Today Review the selected day, add entries to meal sections, remove mistakes Add Create reusable food products Products Browse and search saved food products

docs.title: 1. Create a product
docs.text:
Before you can log meals, you need at least one saved product.

  1. Open the Add screen.
  2. Enter a product name.
  3. Enter a serving label such as 100 g.
  4. Fill in Kcal, Protein, Fat, and Carbs.
  5. Click Save Product.

Note

Nutrition values are stored as non-negative numbers. The default serving label is 100 g.

docs.title: 2. Log food into a meal section
docs.text:
1. Open the Today screen.
  2. Find the meal section where the entry belongs.
  3. Click +.
  4. Select a saved product.
  5. Enter the amount in grams.
  6. Submit the dialog.

The app creates a day entry, recalculates totals, and refreshes the summary automatically.

docs.title: 3. Review daily progress
docs.text:
The summary card on top of the Today screen shows:

  • consumed calories
  • remaining calories
  • daily progress in percent
  • consumed protein, fat, and carbs
  • target values for the tracked nutrients

Current built-in daily targets:

Metric Target Calories 1600 kcal Protein 120 g Fat 53 g Carbs 160 g

docs.title: 4. Use the calendar and meal groups
docs.text:
Nutrio groups entries by calendar day and shows them in these sections:

  • Breakfast
  • Snack
  • Lunch
  • Second Snack
  • Dinner
  • Third Snack

Use the calendar at the top of the app to switch between days and inspect previous totals.

docs.title: 5. Remove an incorrect entry
docs.text:
1. Open the correct day on the Today screen.
  2. Find the meal card containing the wrong entry.
  3. Click Delete.
  4. Wait for the summary to refresh.

docs.title: 6. Browse products
docs.text:
Open the Products screen to:

  • inspect all saved products
  • search by product name
  • compare nutrition values quickly before logging a meal

docs.title: 7. How data separation works
docs.text:
Nutrio does not use sign-in. Instead, the frontend generates a browser-specific deviceId and stores it in localStorage under the key nutrio:deviceId.

Practical consequences:

  • your data is separated per browser profile
  • clearing browser storage can make old data appear disconnected
  • opening the app in another browser creates a different identity

docs.title: 8. Privacy expectations
docs.text: Nutrio stores food products and day entries in PostgreSQL. Data is not anonymous from an infrastructure perspective, but the current product uses browser-generated identity rather than named user accounts.
